target: dialog open state and modal versus nonmodal presentation
observed_behavior: The HTML Standard defines dialog as a transitory task/information window; its boolean open attribute indicates an active dialog. The HTMLDialogElement.show() algorithm displays a nonmodal dialog, whereas showModal() calls the modal-show algorithm, marking the dialog modal and arranging top-layer presentation. A dialog already open in the other mode can trigger InvalidStateError under the documented method guards. Changing open alone is not equivalent to all method-defined lifecycle steps.
context: W07 B2 K3 read-only observation; WHATWG HTML Living Standard authoritative for the described native HTML mechanisms and guarded algorithms only; source shows Last Updated 20 July 2026.
limitations: The modal/nonmodal distinction concerns the native dialog algorithms, not any element styled visually as a dialog.
show() and showModal() include specific state checks; presence of open by itself does not establish is-modal/top-layer state.
The source advises against manual open-attribute removal because modal document blocking and close-event semantics may be left inconsistent.
HTML algorithms are normative platform definitions, not observations of a browser or endorsement of one application design.
